# Raw terminal fragmentation corpus (version 1)

The `.bin` files are literal bytes, not escaped strings. `manifest.json` records
lengths and SHA-256 hashes so other terminal adapters can reuse exactly the same
input. No external processes, files, clipboard reads, or network requests are
performed by these terminal-state tests. The OSC52 fixture queues requests only.

Run the production-parser suite with:

    cargo test --locked --lib terminal::fragmentation_tests

Each small fixture runs as one read, at every two-way cut including empty reads,
as byte-at-a-time input, and under 100 deterministic xorshift64 partitions (seeds
1 through 100; maximum chunk 23). The combined stream excludes the final RIS reset
fixture so that reset cannot hide preceding differences (maximum chunk 31).
Seeds, input, and cut offsets reproduce failures. Oversize input is generated by
the manifest's byte recipe rather than checking in a 4 MiB binary. Its 100 seeded
partitions use maximum chunk 128 KiB, plus introducer, limit±1 and ST boundaries;
all 4 million two-way cuts are intentionally not enumerated. There are no new
random/fuzz dependencies. Typical native debug runtime is about 14 seconds.

The semantic snapshot compares both grids and cell attributes, wraps/history,
cursor/save state, modes, replies, title/colors, hyperlink targets, clipboard
requests, pending parser bytes, command identities/anchors/provenance/output,
and the corpus's Kitty image pixels/placements. Batch-specific dirty versions,
caches, wall/monotonic clocks, locally measured command duration, and global
image revision counters are excluded. Mutation negative controls verify that
grid, modes, replies and command identity changes are detected. This is a
metamorphic production-parser oracle, not an independent terminal implementation.
The UTF-8 replacement tests additionally use `String::from_utf8_lossy` as an
independent maximal-subpart reference. No external VTE compatibility is claimed.

## Limits and malformed input

- Pending escape cap: 4 MiB, including APC introducer and terminator. Complete and
  fragmented Kitty APCs must enforce the same limit before graphics dispatch.
- Kitty control cap: 16 KiB excluding the `G` discriminator. Recovery includes one
  extra byte for that discriminator so a final `q=2` is preserved.
- OSC8 parameters: 256 bytes; URI limit is the pinned shared link limit.
- OSC52 decoded clipboard: 100 KiB; oversized clipboard contents are rejected.
- Every test read checks all pending buffers stay within the pending cap.
- Overflowed Kitty APCs discard until ST or CAN/SUB cancellation. Tests check
  one bounded rejection, quiet replies, no repeated replies while discarding,
  no invented command completion, and recovery of following text.
- Existing OSC/DCS overflow policy is different: drop the overflowing read and
  return to ground. Subsequent payload bytes can print, so inputs beyond this
  limit are explicitly **not** claimed partition-invariant. A characterization
  verifies the difference and equal recovery after explicit RIS.
- `aborted.bin` exercises an incomplete OSC interrupted by CAN, then RIS from
  alternate-screen/running-command state, restoring ordinary text and queries.
  This is parser/reset recovery, not a persisted-session restore test.
- Incomplete valid UTF-8 prefixes remain pending at read boundaries. An ASCII
  continuation probe makes replacement observable without treating read EOF as
  stream EOF. Invalid leads, overlong sequences, surrogates and out-of-range
  scalars are checked against the standard library across every cut.
